page: Microsoft Azure E16ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores via an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. Its cache hierarchy features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 480 MB L3 cache. System memory totals 128 GB, establishing an allocation of 8 GB RAM per vCPU. Processor flags include support for AVX-512 vector extensions, AMX tile and int8 matrices, and AES cryptography acceleration. Storage is provided by an integrated 945 GB local NVMe SSD, while GPU hardware is omitted entirely.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong compression throughput alongside balanced general performance. The processor achieved top-tier throughput in single-threaded compression tests, reaching 36.52 GB/s in gzip and 15.37 GB/s in bzip3 decompression, alongside small-model LLM generation rates of 343.48 tokens per second. Multi-core compute benchmarks, including stress-ng and PassMark CPU evaluations, sit within the middle tier. In-memory data handling is consistent, demonstrating 136.15 GB/s uncached large-block read bandwidth, 56.03 GB/s write bandwidth, and over 32 million Redis SET operations per second.

From an architectural standpoint, the E16ds_v7 couples dense memory with bundled local NVMe storage, delivering high operational value for stateful applications that benefit from low-latency scratch space without relying entirely on remote volumes. The primary tradeoff is the 2:1 hyperthreaded core topology, which shares execution pipelines under concurrent execution. This server profile is well fitted for in-memory databases, Redis caching layers, ETL data processing, and relational database management systems requiring high memory capacity.
description: Microsoft Azure E16ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine configured with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor reaching clock speeds of 4.2 GHz. Built on Microsoft Hyper-V with x86_64 architecture, the instance provides 128 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a substantial 480 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 945 GB of local NVMe SSD storage for high-speed scratch space and temporary file operations, with zero attached GPUs. Compute features include hardware support for AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets, contributing to top-tier single-threaded compression performance in gzip and bzip3 benchmarks. Memory bandwidth and multi-core processing metrics rank in the middle tier, with Redis handling over 32 million SET operations per second. The instance provides a balanced resource configuration for memory-heavy deployments such as Redis caching layers, relational databases, enterprise resource planning systems, and large-scale data analytics.
